# Exact depth at the central centroid of symmetric simplex chains

This is a completed restricted structural theorem. The base has one
integer coordinate, the fibers are homothetic simplices with a common
vertex, and their radii are symmetric about the half-integer1/2. No
reduction of arbitrary mixed-integer convex bodies to this class is
asserted.

## Theorem and definitions

Let d>=1, m>=0, and let

    T_d={x in R^d:x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=1}, V_d=1/d!,
    R=r_0>0, r_0>=r_1>=...>=r_m>=0.

Assume the successive drops r_(h-1)-r_h are nondecreasing. At the
integer bases -h and h+1, for h=0,...,m, put the fibers r_h T_d.
Let S be their disjoint union, let mu be their summed d-dimensional
Lebesgue measure, and put Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. Then the single point

    y=(0,R/(d+1),...,R/(d+1)) in S

satisfies, for EVERY closed ambient halfspace H containing y,

    mu(S intersect H)>=(Gamma_d/2)mu(S).

The piecewise affine interpolation of the paired radii is nonnegative
and concave on[-m,m+1]. Thus

    C={ (z,x):-m<=z<=m+1, x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=r(z) }

is a convex body, and S=C intersect(Z times R^d). Its intrinsic
Hausdorff dimension is d because the central radius is positive;
mu=H_d on S. Zero terminal radii contribute zero H_d-measure. The
constant Gamma_d/2 is sharp within this class already when m=0.

## Proved inputs and dependency boundary

The following sources contain complete proofs of the inputs used here.
All inputs have independent audits recorded in the worktree.

1. `candidate cebdfbe6dc0c0994`:
   for one fixed normalized positive normal u and fixed tilt -beta, an
   affine radius sequence ell_h=R-alpha h weakly decreases EACH paired
   deficit F_(r_h)(t-beta h)+F_(r_h)(t+beta(h+1))-Gamma_d r_h^d.
   It preserves R, y, u, beta, the original bases, and their number.
2. `candidate 0722a9c9ad369925`:
   every finite affine-radius chain satisfies the desired cap inequality
   when max u_i>=2/(d+1). It includes d=1 and repeated normal coordinates.
   Its proof uses the exact conditional simplex law and the proved
   two-list counting inequality, not a relaxed mean constraint.
3. `candidate 8704554a92158bfc`: if all barycentric
   coordinates lambda_i of a simplex point are at most1/d, its ordinary
   halfspace depth is min_i d^d product_(j!=i)lambda_j. Its proof includes
   coefficient coincidences and points on the region's boundary.
4. `candidate 3f7ae72f2c829951`:
   for d>=3 and max u_i<=2/(d+1), a simplex cap through its centroid
   has normalized mass at least(7/6)Gamma_d. This is now unconditional:
   the last scalar input was proved in
   `candidate 93a759825a881af9`
   and independently audited by root, Minkowski, and Simplex.
5. `candidate e06a5b80357a8187`:
   with t=1/(d+1), a>0, 0<=beta<=at, r_h=(1-ah)_+,

       E_d(q,r)=d^d q^(d-1)(r-dq)_+,

   interpreted as zero when r=0, its full finite sum satisfies

       sum_h [E_d(t-beta h,r_h)+E_d(t+beta(h+1),r_h)]
          >Gamma_d sum_h r_h^d-Gamma_d/6.

   Every positive-radius argument q is positive. The source proves all
   slope edges, compact attainment, escaping-slope limits, and knot bounds.
6. `candidate dd382d5b121a0508`:
   in dimension2 the same full sum has loss at most4/81, and the own
   centroid cap with max u_i<=2/3 has mass at least1/2=Gamma_2+1/18.

Inputs1 and2 use the ordinary continuous Grünbaum inequality. The
probability input4 retains its fixed negative unit coefficient and has
no assumed localization or rounding lemma. No input is a general
mixed-integer centerpoint assertion. The remaining steps are proved
explicitly below.

## 1. Every continuous normal reduces to a nonnegative one

Tighten any containing halfspace to pass through y. This only decreases
its mass. If its continuous normal is zero, a closed halfspace in the
base line contains at least one entire member of each reflected pair.
Its mass is at least half the total, which is sufficient.

Otherwise write its margin as

    b z+v dot x-t sum_i v_i, t=R/(d+1), v!=0.

If v is already nonnegative, divide by its positive coordinate sum.
If some coordinate is negative, choose i with v_i=min_j v_j<0. On
each individual fiber rT_d apply the measure-preserving barycentric swap

    x'_i=r-sum_j x_j, x'_j=x_j for j!=i.

It maps that simplex bijectively to itself. Define

    w_i=-v_i>0, w_j=v_j-v_i>=0 for j!=i.

The transformed original margin equals

    b z+w dot x'+v_i r-t sum_j v_j.

Since sum_j w_j=sum_j v_j-(d+1)v_i and r<=R, the genuine ambient
halfspace margin

    b z+w dot x'-t sum_j w_j

is the preceding expression plus v_i(R-r), hence is no larger.
Its cap on every fiber is contained in the swapped original cap,
and it passes through the SAME y. Dividing by sum_j w_j>0 produces
a normalized nonnegative normal. The fiberwise swaps are only changes
of integration variables; they are not asserted to form an ambient
affine lattice transformation.

It consequently suffices to prove the lower bound for every normalized
u>=0 with sum u_i=1 and every base tilt b.

## 2. The smaller sign of the tilt

For each pair let F_h(s) be its d-volume in the continuous cap
u dot x>=t+s, divided by V_d. It is nonincreasing in s. For beta>=0
the mass with tilt +beta minus the mass with tilt -beta is the sum of

    F_h(beta h)+F_h(-beta(h+1))
       -F_h(-beta h)-F_h(beta(h+1))
    =[F_h(-beta(h+1))-F_h(-beta h)]
       +[F_h(beta h)-F_h(beta(h+1))]>=0.

Thus it suffices to treat the actual oblique halfspace

    -beta z+u dot x>=t, beta>=0.

No fiber has been separately re-centered and no tilt has been selected
independently on different fibers.

## 3. Affine radii and the easy range

Put F_r(q)=vol_d(rT_d intersect{u dot x>=q})/V_d. The total normalized
mass is2 sum_h r_h^d, so the desired deficit is

    sum_h [F_(r_h)(t-beta h)+F_(r_h)(t+beta(h+1))-Gamma_d r_h^d].

For m=0 its own left cap already contributes at least Gamma_d R^d
by ordinary Grünbaum. For m>=1 apply input1. It provides nonnegative
affine radii R-alpha h and weakly decreases every displayed summand.
A violating original cap would therefore give a violating affine cap
with the same y and halfspace. It remains to exclude all affine violations.

Scale every continuous coordinate by1/R; this preserves the integer
base and all normalized masses. Now R=1, t=1/(d+1), and r_h=1-ah.
If beta>=at, then

    t-beta h<=t(1-ah)=t r_h.

Each left cap contains its own simplex centroid and contributes at
least Gamma_d r_h^d. This proves the result termwise, including a=0,
beta=at, and zero radii.

The only remaining range is a>0 and0<=beta<at. If max u_i>=2/(d+1),
input2 proves the result directly for every finite affine prefix. This
includes the whole d=1 case, where necessarily u_1=1.

## 4. A violating finite affine prefix extends to a violating full leg

For positive r_h=1-ah in the remaining range, write its paired cap
fraction as

    c_h=F_1((t-beta h)/r_h)+F_1((t+beta(h+1))/r_h).

Both thresholds increase with real h while r_h>0: their derivatives
are respectively(at-beta)/r_h^2 and[beta+a(t+beta)]/r_h^2, which are
positive. Consequently c_h is nonincreasing.

If a finite prefix had negative weighted deficit
sum_h r_h^d(c_h-Gamma_d), its last positive-radius term would have
c_h<Gamma_d. Every appended positive-radius term would then also
have strictly negative deficit. Extending to all h>=0 with1-ah>0
would preserve the violation. This extension is finite since a>0.
Terms at zero radius contribute exactly zero. It therefore suffices
to prove the cap bound on the full leg r_h=(1-ah)_+.

## 5. Universal diagonal envelope and the own-cap bonus

For any r>0 and q>=r/(d+1),

    F_r(q)>=E_d(q,r)=d^d q^(d-1)(r-dq)_+.

For q>=r/d the right side is zero. Otherwise the point q times the
all-one vector lies in rT_d and has barycentric coordinates

    q/r,...,q/r, 1-dq/r.

They are all at most1/d. Moreover q/r>=1/(d+1) makes the last
coordinate no larger than each of the others. Input3 gives its
ordinary depth d^d(q/r)^(d-1)(1-dq/r). The cap u dot x>=q passes
through that point because sum u_i=1. Multiplying the depth by r^d
proves the envelope. The zero-radius interpretation is immediate.

In the hard-tilt range, every positive radius satisfies

    t-beta h>=t r_h>0,
    t+beta(h+1)>=t r_h>0.

Thus the envelope applies at every original threshold of the full leg.
Its own left term is exactly E_d(t,1)=Gamma_d.

For d>=3 in the remaining normal range max u_i<=2/(d+1), input4
improves that ONE own term to at least Gamma_d+Gamma_d/6. Applying
input5 to all other terms as well as the own envelope gives

    full actual paired cap sum
      >=sum_h [E_d(t-beta h,r_h)+E_d(t+beta(h+1),r_h)]
          +Gamma_d/6
      >Gamma_d sum_h r_h^d.

The bonus is counted only once, at base0. Both members of every pair
remain in the sum. The strict kernel estimate is the reason this
bonus suffices with the exact target constant.

For d=2, input6 instead gives

    full paired cap sum>=Gamma_2 sum_h r_h^2-4/81+1/18
       =Gamma_2 sum_h r_h^2+1/162.

This covers the remaining low-maximum normal sector in dimension2.
Dimension1 was covered in Section3, so all continuous dimensions are
now exhausted. Section4 excludes every violating finite affine prefix,
and Section3 excludes every violating original concave radius chain.

## 6. Boundary cases, membership, and sharpness

The selected point is the centroid of the positive actual base0 fiber,
so it belongs to S. Every step retains that point. The scalar scaling
changes only continuous coordinates and tracks the common volume
factor R^d. The tilt comparison uses the actual integer labels -h,h+1.
Every normalized nonvertical halfspace has a measure-zero boundary in
each positive d-dimensional fiber; vertical halfspaces include entire
boundary fibers and were counted separately. Terminal point fibers
have zero H_d mass since d>=1. No limiting candidate is selected.

For m=0 there are exactly two equal simplex fibers at0 and1. The
proved lower bound is Gamma_d/2. Conversely, any point of a simplex
has a barycentric coordinate at least1/(d+1). The cap toward that
vertex through the point has relative volume at most Gamma_d.
A sufficiently large finite base tilt isolates its own fiber and
excludes the other fiber while preserving this cap. Its normalized
mass in S is at most Gamma_d/2. Thus the maximum depth is exactly
Gamma_d/2 for this example.

In continuous dimension zero, the corresponding paired interval of
integer points {-m,...,m+1} has counting depth exactly1/2 at0 or1:
each closed halfline through0 contains at least m+1 of its2m+2
points, and the left halfline attains that number. This is a separate
counting statement; no radius to the zeroth power is used above.

The theorem proves all ambient halfspaces for the stated class. It
does not assert a centroid selection for nonsymmetric chains, a
localization of general fibers to simplices, or a reduction in the
number of integer coordinates.
